svg.title: Lab 03 — DHCP, PAT and an ISP edge
svg.desc: Clients lease addresses from Router0, then share one public address through PAT to reach a server behind an ISP
svg.text: Lab 03 — DHCP, PAT and an ISP edge
Clients lease addresses from Router0, then share one public address through PAT to reach a server behind an ISP
NAT TABLE ON ROUTER0 (SHOW IP NAT TRANSLATIONS)
ISP has no route back to 192.168.1.0/24 — and shouldn't
Private addresses never cross the edge; only 203.0.113.1 is visible
NAT table maps it back to the right PC
Clear the NAT table, browse again and compare how the inside-global port changes while the inside-local port stays put.
DHCP supplies address + mask + gateway; PAT then makes those private addresses usable on the public side.
